facts.text: Herriman sprang to life in spring 1851 when Mormon pioneers Henry Herriman, Thomas Butterfield, John Jay Stocking, and Robert Cowan Petty settled the area.
A fort once stood where the community garden now sits, and today only two black locust trees mark its former entrance.
After a door‑to‑door petition, residents secured municipal incorporation on June 1 1999, turning Herriman from an unincorporated settlement into a city.
No railroad or major industry ever reached Herriman, preserving its rural character with scattered homesteads linked by dirt roads.
Herriman sits within the Salt Lake City metropolitan area, located in southwestern Salt Lake County.
In 2022 the city annexed the 933‑acre Olympia development on its west side, expanding its boundaries significantly.
